items.title: Default: ecology cadence 1,500 -> 3,000 ticks
items.detail: The sweep found no effect of the ecology pass cadence on a wolf pack against herds 45-60 tiles away, in both cell orders. A 3,000-tick default halves the passes and their fuse time at no measured cost. Not applied to v7.0 (cfg.ecology.cadence is still 1500).
items.evidence: SW1+SW1R, 4 reps: wolf attacks on placed herds ctl 174, cad500 243, cad6000 145; placed prey killed 1/2/0
items.next: On a yes, set ecology.cadence=3000 in the v7.0 defaults, add a changelog line and a validator default check; include in SW8.

items.title: Default: ecology nudge off
items.detail: Neither the current nudge (40 tiles / 3,000 t / r6) nor a tighter one changed kills or attacks against off, once cell order was controlled. RELS shows DF brings the fight itself once a relation exists, and off means no visible teleports. Not applied (ecology.nudge=true).
items.evidence: SW1+SW1R pooled: nudge_off 179 attacks / 3 placed kills vs ctl 174 / 1; nudge_tight 198 / 1
items.next: On a yes, default ecology.nudge=false; keep the `groups nudge` verb for players who want it.

items.title: Default: pack_sneak 0 and retire the per-unit SNEAK write
items.detail: Sneak bonus 0 / 0.25 / 1.0 made no measurable difference in either cell order, matching STL/STL2 (wild AI never hides). Setting pack_sneak 0 removes one class of unit writes; the 0.05 pack-mass floor stays because the arena cannot isolate it from DF's own aiming of placed units.
items.evidence: SW2+SW2R placed prey killed over 4 reps: ctl 4, sneak0 4, sneak100 0; STL/STL2 hidden 0 of 426 samples
items.next: Set v7.pack_sneak=0 and delete the unit SNEAK write path in ecoWrite; update mech.v70.pack_sneak claim.

items.detail: SW7 rosters built with bonus 1, 3 and 5 gave the same land groups and fights on CTRL; design rule R11 already treats the x3 as a contrived weight. The rig test was weak (only 7-8 of 27-29 wanted species exist in CTRL's pool), while the desk D1 shows rosters change at every level (pack-hunt presence 57% -> 77%).
items.evidence: SW7: land groups 3.1/1.6 (x1), 2.2/2.2 (x3), 3.3/2.8 (x5), attacks 0 in all cells; D1: 100% of CTRL keys change
items.next: On a yes, drop ROSTER.packBonus and roster2.py pack_pref, rerun run2.py to restate v2.2 metrics.

items.title: Drop the apex step from the FREQUENCY ladder; steer apexes by placement and stock
items.detail: The apex FREQUENCY does not visibly bring apexes: 0 apex arrivals in all 4 CTRL season runs, 0-3 elsewhere, and apex present in 1 of 6 SW4 runs at any predator multiplier. Steering apexes then needs a mechanism the tool lacks today: a placed or stocked apex group (one LP group per map, two on savage maps, design R12.7).
items.evidence: S8C/S8Cb CTRL apex 0,0,0,0; S8B 0,3 cheetah; S8O 2,1 anaconda; SW4 apex present 1 of 6
items.next: Decide yes/no; if yes, design an apex placement/stock job (cadence, max groups, season gate) and remove AL/AW from ROSTER.LADDER.

items.detail: Caps of 1 and 2 cut the tool's own cavern groups by about 40% but never approach the cap, because DF's native cavern populations (4-5 groups per depth) are not the tool's to gate. The Layers tab presents it as a ceiling, which misleads.
items.evidence: SW5: cavern groups 24.0/27.3 at auto vs 13.7-16.0 at caps 1 and 2, same in both orders
items.next: Reword the Layers tab and `limits` output ('target for the tool's own cavern groups'); keep auto.

items.title: Should carnivorous swimmers count as scavengers?
items.detail: SCAV.is counts a scavenger only if it is BONECARN, a CURIOUS_BEAST_EATER or on SCAV.TEXT; among vanilla swimmers that leaves only POND_GRABBER, SEA_SERPENT and SEA_MONSTER, so alligators, crocodiles and sharks never scavenge and scav_ext's swimmer path has almost no vanilla users. Water carcasses were cleared in SCV2Wb with pond grabbers or wolves on the bank.
items.evidence: SCV2Wb: 6 -> 0 carp carcasses in all 4 cells; SCVW: alligators walked 0 of 5
items.next: Ask the user; if yes, add CARNIVORE + aquatic/semiaquatic (or a curated list) to SCAV.is and rerun a water cell with crocodiles.

items.title: Group-size cap for animal people (plump helmet men) in caverns
items.detail: With the builder on, plump helmet men filled the cavern shore-prey slot and arrived about 15 per wave, 54 and 180 units in a season on BOATS (33 died in rep 1). The ladder sets wave share, not unit share, so a large-cluster species swamps the layer. A cap via cfg.group_size (the mechanism v7 outgun_cap already writes) is the obvious lever.
items.evidence: S8B BOATS: PLUMP_HELMET_MAN 54 and 180 units, 7 and 12 waves
items.next: Ask the user for the rule (cap for animal-person/civ prey, e.g. <=5, or ladder divided by mean cluster); build it behind a v7 switch and rerun S8B one rep.

items.detail: With CENOZOIC_SMILODON's population entry added on calm CTRL, DF drew none in a full season in either replicate, so Add invasive cannot rely on DF's draw for SAVAGE species. Options: place them with the headless placement path (dfhack.units.create + six writes), or refuse SAVAGE species on calm maps with an explanation. Not built.

items.title: Arena blocks: make counterbalancing the default and isolate the tool's write from DF's aiming
items.detail: Cells sharing one load pick up natives over time, so position decided the 'busy' flags in SW1/SW2. Counterbalancing (even reps reversed) is opt-in and set only for SW3-SW7. Placed units are non-wild to DF (RELS row 3), which aims them itself, so arena cells cannot separate the tool's written pair from DF's (why SW2 could not test the pack floor). With 2 reps, reversal balances position but does not remove the pile-up.
items.evidence: SW1/SW1R placed-wolf share ~90% first cell vs ~22% last
items.next: Default counterbalance on for every multi-cell block; prefer a fresh load per arm (as VRM2) for arena blocks; read DF's rel rows in arena cells.

items.title: Animal people carry their root animal's mass in the builder's species table
items.detail: species2.tsv gives each animal person its root animal's body size, but every ANIMAL_PERSON variation applies GRAVITATE_BODY_SIZE:70000, which pulls the in-game size toward 70,000 cm³. So a damselfly man reads 10 cm³ in the builder. Size bands, the 5% pack-mass floor and prey choice for all 185 animal people rest on the wrong mass. 64 species also disagree between species2 and the raws (tiny bugs, their giants, ANT_MAN castes).
items.evidence: raws figure 11: 4 animal people of bug roots have no prey

items.title: 19 animal people round to FREQUENCY 0 and may never spawn
